Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for HalcyonAI — sizing questions

Hi Maya — great to hear the timeline. Looping in Vivek (capacity/ops) and Neha (CS/SLA) to scope the handoff.

High level proposal from Redwood:
- Initial pool: 4 worker nodes (A100-80GB equiv) sized for ~200 steady concurrent tokens/sec; autoscale to 8 workers for bursts.
- Burst policy: automatic scale when 95th-percentile latency exceeds 220ms or queue depth > 30 requests; cooldown 10 minutes. Metric-driven burst (not time-window-only) to reduce cost.
- Regional topology: primary us-west, synchronous failover to us-east; cross-region warm cache for most-recent prefix (short-lived KV cache during failover).
- Security: we'll provide SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration doc; ops requires a signed PO for Dedicated activation.

I've attached a capacity template to capture expected endpoints, model choices, and sequence length distribution — please fill and return. Once we have that we can produce a formal proposal and MAP.

Next steps I propose:
1) Discovery call this week (30m) to review the attached template and confirm models/endpoints.
2) Redwood ops to draft pool topology and provisioning window.
3) Delivery of MAP and cost delta for burst usage.

Attachments: halcyon_capacity_template.xlsx

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity for HalcyonAI — initial ops plan

Team — putting down an ops-centric checklist and an initial pool topology proposal so CS has something to share back.

Operations notes / recommendations:
- Recommended GPU: H100-80GB where available; fallback to A100-80GB depending on region procurement. We'll document perf variance.
- Pool topology: 4 primary workers + 2 hot-standby; autoscale to +4 (total 8) during sustained spikes. Hot-standby reduces cold-start risk during fast failover.
- Warm caching: enable prefix/KV cache for the top 3 endpoints; cross-region replication of cache metadata only — KV content remains local and is rebuilt on failover with warmup scripts.
- Pre-warm strategy: progressive traffic ramping + synthetic load to populate KV cache prior to public launch.
- Maintenance window: propose provisioning during a 3-hour window (low-traffic, weekend preferred) — ops will need final sign-off from Halcyon.
- Cost note: burst to 8 nodes estimated +40% incremental for peak periods; we'll provide a 30/60/90 day burn estimate once model selection is final.

I've attached a quick topology diagram and a short checklist for procurement (IP allowlist, KMS fingerprints, networking routes). Ben — please take ownership of the implementation timeline when we confirm the MAP.

Attachments: pool_topology_diagram.png

Thanks,
Vivek
Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
